findings.affected_requirement: FR-011, FR-034, FR-040; plan AD-3/AD-9; data-model sections 1 and 4; prepared-scan-contracts replay identity
findings.evidence: Replay recomputes CodeGraph and Java proof hashes from the caller-supplied package and checks those supplied hashes, but the durable model stores only CodeGraphProofIdentityHash, JavaReadinessIdentityHash, and durations. The migration likewise creates no columns/table for the stable typed proof fields required by data-model.md:97-103. Consequently PostgreSQL cannot independently reconstruct either proof envelope from durable typed values as plan.md:104, plan.md:260, FR-040, and the prepared store contract require. ManifestMatches then compares the stored opaque hashes at lines 373-374 and omits canonical manifest scalars such as SchemaIdentity, CandidateCount, EligibleCount, FilteredCount, SkippedCount, and ApprovalState, so corruption of those persisted identity inputs can still return Replay. The current PostgreSQL qualification mutates the supplied package and one stored Code Unit/audit association, but has no stored typed-proof or manifest-scalar tamper case; the focused PreparedScanAtomicReplayTests pass 5/5 while leaving this relational reconstruction gap unobserved.
findings.correction_outcome: Persist every stable CodeGraphCompletenessProof and JavaReadinessProof canonical preimage field in typed PostgreSQL columns or owned proof principals, update migration/configuration/model snapshot, and reconstruct both proof digests plus the complete manifest fingerprint from stored rows during replay. Compare all canonical manifest scalars and return Conflict on any stored preimage/hash mismatch. Add PostgreSQL regression cases that tamper one stable field in each proof and representative omitted manifest scalars while retaining the old opaque hashes, proving conflict and zero mutation; retain duration-only replay variance.

summary: REVISE. The pinned Story 12.2 boundary preserves the approved Windows-host architecture, exact-revision acquisition, hard CodeGraph/JDT-LS readiness, bounded safe XML, deterministic selection, authorization, transaction rollback, and Story 12.3 exclusions. However, the durable schema does not retain the stable typed CodeGraph or Java readiness proof fields promised by FR-011/FR-034 and AD-3, and replay trusts opaque stored proof hashes plus several unchecked manifest scalars instead of independently reconstructing the complete canonical package required by FR-040/AD-9. This is a HIGH restart/replay integrity defect: persisted corruption or incompatible state can be accepted as mutation-free Replay. The focused atomic replay suite passed 5/5 but does not exercise stored proof/scalar tampering, so it cannot close the defect. No security boundary bypass, source leakage, Worker dispatch, Document generation, CodeGraphContext use, or unrelated architecture regression was otherwise found. The correction is implementation-owned and invalidates convergence and quality review.
